text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher says: "Syria and Israel indicated they want resumption of talks."
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on the eve of a visit to Washington renews his obstinate positions and rejection of the peace commitments of the previous Labour government.

- Syria and Tunisia hold economic talks in Damascus to bolster cooperation in trade exchange and discuss setting a fodder factory in Syria, cotton yarn plants in Syria and Tunisia and a company for international trade according to Syrian and Tunisian laws.
- While condemnation of the double-faced American policy continues, world capitals say: the buffer zone in northern Iraq is a project of division and Turkey risks its regional and international ties.
- Washington threatens militarily and fails diplomatically while fierce battles continue in northern Iraq.
